questions.question: Why are ice cream trucks hazardous to other drivers?

options.text: Ice cream trucks must stay cold.
Children often run toward ice cream trucks without checking for traffic.
Ice cream trucks leave water and ice on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Children often run toward ice cream trucks without checking for traffic.
questions.explanation: Ice cream trucks attract children. Children may run toward them without watching for other vehicles on the road.

questions.question: What is the minimum tread depth required for rear tires?
questions.explanation: Front tires need at least 4/32 of an inch of tread depth. Rear tires need at least 2/32 of an inch of tread depth. All tires on a vehicle should be the same size.

questions.question: What do drivers often do when stuck behind a slow-moving vehicle?
questions.explanation: Drivers commonly tailgate slow-moving vehicles. If someone is tailgating you, let them pass.

questions.question: Tanks typically have:
questions.explanation: Tanks have high centers of gravity. Drivers should be careful when turning or taking curves.

questions.question: What may rust around wheel nuts indicate?
questions.explanation: Check your tires before every drive. Rust around wheel nuts may mean they are loose.

questions.question: Which is NOT a sign of a tired driver?
questions.explanation: Signs of fatigue include trouble focusing, frequent blinking, heavy eyelids, yawning, rubbing eyes, daydreaming, trouble remembering miles driven, missing exits or signs, trouble holding head up, drifting from lanes, following too closely, hitting shoulder rumble strips, and feeling restless or irritable.

questions.question: What is the average driver's reaction time?
questions.explanation: The average driver's reaction time is between 3/4 of a second and one second. At 55 mph, you travel 61 feet during this time.

questions.question: After changing a tire, you should stop a short distance away to:

options.text: Check if the lug nuts are tight.
Make sure the tire is clean.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check if the lug nuts are tight.
questions.explanation: After changing a tire, stop a short distance later to check that the lug nuts are still tight.

questions.question: What is true about combination vehicles?

options.text: They are usually shorter than single commercial vehicles.
They usually require less skill to drive.
They usually require more skill to drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: They usually require more skill to drive.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles require more skill to drive than single commercial vehicles. They are longer, heavier, and more likely to roll over.

questions.question: Why should you perform pre-trip inspection steps in the same order each time?

options.text: You will be less likely to forget something.
You will have more time to complete the inspection.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will be less likely to forget something.
questions.explanation: Using the same order for each inspection helps you remember all the steps. You will be less likely to miss something when you follow a set checklist.

questions.question: ____ is an example of required emergency equipment.
questions.explanation: Commercial motor vehicles must have emergency equipment. This includes spare electrical fuses, three red reflective triangles or three liquid burning flares, and at least one charged fire extinguisher.

questions.question: What is the Johnson bar?

options.text: A hand valve that works the trailer brakes
A valve that indicates the fuel level
A valve that limits the amount of cargo

questions.correctAnswerText: A hand valve that works the trailer brakes
questions.explanation: The Johnson bar (also called the trolley valve) is a hand valve that controls the trailer brakes. Use it only to test the brakes. Using it while driving can cause the vehicle to skid.

questions.question: Rough acceleration:

options.text: Is common if a vehicle is warmed up.
Is encouraged to improve gas mileage.

questions.explanation: Speed up smoothly and gradually. Rough acceleration can cause mechanical damage to the vehicle.

questions.question: When driving in wet conditions, a lack of spray from the tires of other vehicles means:

options.text: Ice has formed on the road.
The spray is caught on the underside of the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ice has formed on the road.
questions.explanation: In wet conditions, no spray from other vehicles' tires means ice has formed on the road. Drive carefully in wet, freezing weather.

questions.question: Why should the steps of a pre-trip inspection be done in the same order each time?

options.text: Because you will be less likely to forget to check something
Because it is required by law

questions.correctAnswerText: Because you will be less likely to forget to check something
questions.explanation: Do pre-trip inspections the same way every time. This helps you remember to check all important parts.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a type of distraction?
questions.explanation: Driving distractions are physical (reaching for an object), mental (talking with a passenger), or both (using a handheld phone).

questions.question: When checking tires, which of the following should not cause concern?

options.text: Tread of at least 4/32 of an inch on front tires
Radial and bias-ply tires used together

questions.correctAnswerText: Tread of at least 4/32 of an inch on front tires
questions.explanation: Front tires need at least 4/32 inch of tread in every groove. Other tires need at least 2/32 inch of tread. Do not mix radial and bias-ply tires or use mismatched tire sizes.

questions.question: An after-trip inspection should be done:
questions.explanation: Do an after-trip inspection at the end of each trip or day. Complete a vehicle inspection report if required.

questions.question: Fully-loaded rigs:

options.text: Are less likely to roll over than empty rigs.
Are more likely to roll over than empty rigs.
Are just as likely to roll over as empty rigs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are more likely to roll over than empty rigs.
questions.explanation: Fully-loaded rigs roll over more easily than empty rigs because the cargo raises the center of gravity.

questions.question: The trailer hand valve should be used:

options.text: To check the connection between the trailer and tractor.

questions.explanation: The trailer hand valve (Johnson bar or trolley valve) controls the trailer brakes. Use it only to test the brakes. Using it while driving can cause a skid.
